⚔️ Sword VS Bow 🏹

Bow has a big advantage here. Every good archer will be able to land most of their shots on you if you don't know how to move correctly.

🔻How to dodge bow shots?🔻

The archer has to predict where they think you're gonna be to be able to land their shots. Therefore you have to move in a very unpredictable way. Do weird unorthodox movements to the sides, move to each side randomly and for a random amount of time and keep changing your movement patterns while moving forward a bit each time. Mainly do small movements so they'll have less time to catch you with a shot before you change to a your movement direction.
After they release the shot you have a tiny bit of time to rush forward until their bow is charged again and then you repeat what's written above.

If they kite back, each time you see them turn on you to shoot, release W, and choose one direction to go to (holding A or D), after you dodge keep going forward and repeat. This is the best way of dodging when they try to kite.

You can also use your surroundings to your advantage, you can hide behinds blocks, fake it like you're about to move forward, making them miss, then you have time to keep closing the distance.

❌ What to avoid?

  1. Do not try to dodge with jumps, the archer can just wait for you to land and you'll be completely vulnerable to a shot.
  2. When you get close enough to hit them, make sure you use CRITS and avoid using sprinthits completely. Sprinthits can boost them forward increasing the distance between you and them
    .

🗡️ Sword vs Axe 🪓

When using a sword against an axe, you should use any attack that has low kb. Sweeps and crits are extremely effective against axe users, both if they run away or if they try to trade. When they try to trade, use punish crits and normal crit spam methods to out damage them. If they try to run, chase with crits and sweeps. Also dodging their first axe crits is very important as it can really mess them up because they have to go through a huge cooldown. You should also hold W to perform sprint crits and sprint sweeps, this is a very easy method of beating axe, you will out damage any axe user this way in an op kit setting. Combine both methods of dodging arrows and fighting axes if you are fighting a trident!

🗡️ Sword vs Speed 👨‍🔬

Speed users are very tricky to play against if you have no speed. The best way to handle a speed user is to play defensive and make them come to you, then you can get combos and crits on them easier than if you go to them instead. Play carefully against a speed user!

✅ Ping ✅

🚀Control:

  • With low ping you have a lot more control, you can get stuff done with better timing and pull off smooth combos. You also get comboed more easily.

  • With high ping you have a lot less control, a bit harder to land hits and the timing is worse. Delayed kb also makes it harder to aim on you or combo you and it limits you to only using certain techniques cuz most will simply just not work with high ping.

🧑‍🏫 Benefits:

  • High ping benefits worse players more since it allows you to get away with missing hits and not get punished for it because you are naturally harder to combo. Also it allows you to perform well while having bad pvp knowledge or doing things incorrectly.

  • Low ping benefits good players more since usually good players mix up a lot of different kind of techniques that would be unusable with high ping, also they and dont miss many hits and have good timing so its gonna be harder to combo them anyways.

Therefore good players would be better the lower ping they have and bad players would be a lot better with high ping.

If the ping is between 1-100ms, the fights are almost completely fair.
From 100+ it starts becoming awkward.

📈 How to use lag:

As you move with lag, your character model and hitbox have delay server side that makes you further in front or behind than you are on your own screen. this is how "lag reach" is created. When playing with 100+ ms, spamming crits and using s-tap combos is the most effective way to play. S tap combos are easily done in high ping and it abuses ping reach, and crits are easily abusable as you take low kb, delayed kb, or teleport.

📉 How to fight lag:

The best thing you could do is try to adjust your timing to their delay. Also, its alot more crucial to not miss first hits VS lagger, cuz you can get punished a lot harder than you normally would.

Lastly, trying to win trades is more consistent VS laggers than trying to stun them.

⚔️ Components of 1.9 Sword PvP ⚔️

🎯 Aim 🎯

Aim has always been one of the most important things in sword pvp.

🏹 Range Control 🏹

How well you control range, knowing when you're close enough to hit your opponent or to dodge your opponent's hits.
[starting outside of hit range]

🥏Spacing 🥏

How well you can distant yourself from the opponent to get a stun hit.
[starting from hit range]

⏱️Timing ⏱️

Knowing how to time your hits well and the moves / counters you want to go for.

🥊 KB Control 🥊

How well you can control your knockback, utilizing NoKb techniques properly, and understanding scenarios where you can't utilize NoKb techniques and back off in time.

🪃 Combo Control 🪃

How well you control your combos. Knowing how to space within a combo, which technique to use, correct hit timing, or how to move correctly.

🌪️ Movement 🌪️

Knowing how to control your movements properly to make your opponent miss, or to gain the proper amount of range that you need.

🧑‍🏫 Knowledge 🧑‍🏫

Technique usage, Versatility, Playstyle.

🎖️ Adaptation 🎖️

How well you can adapt to different players, pings, different playstyles or different moves that people like to go for, to come out on top.

🏆 Prediction 🏆

Knowing how to read your opponent and knowing what they're gonna do before they do it.

🔻Further Explanations🔻

🧑‍🏫 Adaption 🧑‍🏫

Every player has a different playstyle, different ping, likes to go for certain moves more than others. Adaption is all about changing what YOU do to be able to counter what your opponent does. This requires a lot of PvP knowledge and experience

  • Simple Adaption- Adapting to a specific move that your opponent goes for. For example, if you notice that your opponent goes for NoKb crits in every chance they get, you can start to instantly go for double crits whenever you get critted by them.

  • Advanced Adaption- Recognizing a pattern of moves that your opponent keeps going for. For example, trading patterns, movement patterns etc, and knowing how to adapt to it and counter it.

  • Playstyle Adaption- Changing parts of your playstyle, or changing your playstyle entirely, to be able to beat a specific opponent by adapting to their playstyle.

🧑‍🏫 Baits 🧑‍🏫

Baiting your opponent into going for a certain move then countering it. For example baiting someone to go forward by running into them and then backing away to make them miss, then you have a hit advantage. Or jumping as if you're gonna crit them which baits them into trying to deflect, and then use a falling sprinthit instead to knock them away.

💥 Counters 💥

There is a misconception that you're supposed to beat someone after you "counter" their move, but realistically if they don't mess up, the counter is supposed to get you out of a bad situation with taking minimal damage. Many of the times your opponent might mess up, which gives you a chance to deal good damage to them after you counter their move.

📝 Terms 📝

🔻 Consistent Counters - Will always work against a certain technique.

🔻 Situational Counters - A move that counters what your opponent tries to do, but isn't guaranteed to always work.

My final opinion based on the 5 fights ive seen-

Kyla still hasn't fully peaked-
- She could learn how to use s-crits better, and fix her own weakness to S-crits. [ the reason why she didnt get punished too hard when she got caught by vexay's s-crits is because shes good enough to be able to recover fast from bad situations. s-crits are still the main weakness she has imo]

- She can also get better by recognizing when she's about to get stunned, and hold S in time.

⚔️ Sprinthits ⚔️

Technique Creator - LoCr
Name Creator - LoCr

📝 Stun Technique

Risk ⭐☆☆
Reward ⭐⭐⭐

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

🗡️ Sprinthits deal more knockback and are meant to stun the target:
- If you hold sprint, only the first hit of the combo will be a sprint hit and all the rest will be sweep hits. You need to keep resetting your sprint to be able to keep getting sprinthits with every one of your hits. How come the target gets stunned from a sprint hit combo? When the target gets knocked back by the sprint hit, their range gets lowered, and that allows you to keep on comboing without being touched.

🔻There are a few ways to reset your sprint effectively🔻

1."W-Taps"- Release W and then press it again after every hit to reset the sprinthit. This might be riskier to go for than the next options i'll be giving, since it is usually countered by NoKb moves.

2."Pausing W-Taps"- Pause for a bit before pressing "w" again instead of pressing it right away. This way you will abuse the full knockback, and you can get a better stun on your opponent.

3."S-Taps"- S-Taps give the best stun on the target if done correctly. Since the target loses range while getting knocked back, if you keep s-tapping to 3 block range, your opponent won't be able to touch you.

"Crouch-tap"- Completely useless, but it resets your sprinthit and you can go for a sprinthit combo with it

  • Sprinthit Combo - ⁠You can get sprinthit combos on people with either strafe OR straight-line. You have to maintain 3 block spacing [or close to it] and perfect hit timing to be able to keep the combo.
  • When should you use each form of sprint reset tactic? It is situational and depends on the spacing that you need for your next hit to maintain your stun.

✅ Best Scenarios: Combos
❌ Worst Scenarios: VS Jump Reset, Hit Select

🔻 Clips: S-Tap, W-Tap, Pausing W-Tap🔻

⚔️ Standard Crits ⚔️

Old names: W Release Crits / Normal Crits
Technique Creator - LoCr / Stumpie

📝 Damage Technique

Risk ⭐⭐☆
Reward ⭐⭐☆

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

Jump and hit while falling. Release W every time before you go for a hit (to cancel the sprinthit) this way your hit turns into a crit. You can start critting from the first hit or you can use it in a middle of a combo.

🔻 You can release "W" in different timings, which depends on the situation🔻
Releasing W late will give you a bit more range and a bit more KB reduction, but less control.
Make sure you are jumping from the right distance or else you can get knocked away before you land your hit

✅ Best Scenarios: VS Punish Crit, Double Crit
❌ Worst Scenarios: VS Crit Deflection

⚔️ Crit Deflection ⚔️

Technique Creator - xYuvalx
Name Creator - xYuvalx

📝 Knockaway Technique

Risk ⭐⭐☆
Reward ⭐⭐☆

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

A counter to Standard Crits / Double Crits - Sprinthit the opponent right after they land a crit on you.
If done correctly, they will get knocked away.

✅ Best Scenarios: VS Standard Crits, Double Crits
❌ Worst Scenarios: VS NoKb Crits

⚔️ Punish Crit ⚔️

Name Creator - xYuvalx

📝 Damage Technique

Risk ⭐⭐☆
Reward ⭐☆☆

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

After getting knocked back by a hit, use the knockback as a result, to punish the opponent with a crit (hit while falling from the knockback you just took).

✅ Best Scenarios: Set up for a Double Crit or NoKb Crit.
❌ Worst Scenarios: Using Punish Crits not as a setup for a better technique. This will rarely be good on its own.

⚔️ NoKb Crit ⚔️

Technique Inventor - Unknown
Name Created by - xYuvalx

📝 NoKb Technique

Risk ⭐⭐☆
Reward ⭐⭐⭐

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

A counter to Crit Deflection - After you Crit someone hold W and wait for your opponent to hit you. This way your knockback will be reduced. Only after they hit you, go for your 2nd hit; with your 2nd hit, you can either go for a Punish crit, or for a Falling Sprinthit (which depends on the situation).

1. If you choose to use a "Punish crit" after the opponent hits you, you'll be able to stay on the target and keep your combo going without letting the opponent deflect your crits.
- Make sure you don't go through your opponent [for consistent aim], stop right in front of them instead. Your KB will still be reduced in the same way.
- If your opponent spaces well, you won't be able to get many NoKb Crits in a row

2. By using a "Falling Sprinthit" after the opponent sprinthits you, they will get stunned (if done from the right range), allowing you to keep the combo going. You can also "s-tap" after the "falling sprinthit" when you need some extra space from your opponent to ensure the stun.
- With correct spacing, you can end up stunning somebody no matter how close to them you land. Time your "W" key correctly for that. [can let go of w for a bit to gain more spacing]

✅ Best Scenarios: VS Crit Deflection

❌ Worst Scenarios: VS Double Crits / S-Hold Deflection / Repositioning / Standard Crits

🔻Clips: NoKb Crits, NoKb Crit into Sprinthit Followup, NoKb Crits into S-Hold🔻

⚔️ Double Crit ⚔️

Technique Inventor - Tryh4rdd
Discovered by - xYuvalx
Name Creator - xYuvalx

📝 Damage Technique

Risk ⭐⭐☆
Reward ⭐⭐☆

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

A counter to NoKb Crits - After you get No Kb Critted, use a punish crit and immediately jump again for a Standard Crit.
It ONLY works IF your opponent goes for a punish crit/nokb crits on you. If they sprint hit when you use Double Crit, you will get knocked away.
- It is risky to use a Double Crit on your first hit because this technique can be easily countered. An exception is if you predict your opponent to use a "first hit nokb crit".
- Works VS all ranges, but Best VS Short Range NoKb Crits
Can also strafe with it to try making your opponent miss

✅ Best Scenarios: VS NoKb Crits
❌ Worst Scenarios: VS Standard Crits, Crit Deflection

Risk ⭐⭐☆
Reward ⭐⭐⭐

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

Let someone hit you, and then sprint hit them back immediately. If done correctly, the target will get stunned.

- If you want to maximize the KB reduction, hit the target as fast as you can after you get hit. Best used at longer ranges.
- If you are too close to your opponent, after they hit you, delay your Hit Select to be able to gain enough distance to stun them.

✅ Best Scenarios: VS Sprint hits / S-Hold Deflection. When you're already close to the target, for example in the middle of trades.
❌ Worst Scenarios: Hit selecting from very close range, Hit Selecting on first hits [usually].

Technique Creator - Monkss
Name Creator - Monkss

📝 Stun Technique

Risk ⭐☆☆
Reward ⭐⭐⭐

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

Hit the opponent while jumping forward.

1. Use Uppercuts to cover a long distance in a short amount of time-
- Abuse this when you get a hit advantage while you're in the right distance for an uppercut.
- Catch the opponent by surprise, giving you a chance to stun them and get a combo off.
- Can be also used as a combo extension - whenever someone is about to get out of your combo range or tries to back away from your combo, use an uppercut to close the distance better.

2. Uppercut Combo - [W-Tap / S-Tap uppercut combos, Straightline / Strafe]
- Use uppercuts to combo your opponent. You can combine SOME uppercuts within your combo, or get full combos that consist from uppercuts alone. Uppercut combos probably give the best stun out of any other way of comboing, if performed correctly.

❌ Worst Scenarios: Too close to the opponent

📝 Knockaway Technique

Risk ⭐⭐☆
Reward ⭐⭐⭐

Sprinthit while FALLING.

Risk ⭐⭐☆
Reward ⭐⭐⭐

📋Tap or hold S [depending on the scenario] after critting at a specific timing to get enough distance from your opponent for them to not be able to hit you back, giving you a hit advantage.

🔻 There are 3 ways to use S-Crits depending on the situation🔻

1. A Hit Advantage tool:
Putting yourself in a position where you can hit your opponent while they can't hit you back.

2. A Combo Set Up:
Using S Crits as a tool for spacing to be able to STUN your target.

3. Escape tool:
Escape a dangerous scenario.

❌ Worst Scenarios: When your opponent is too close to the ground [in this scenario they will be able to jump again and crit you out].

Name Creator - xYuvalx

📝 Spacing Technique

Risk ⭐⭐☆
Reward ⭐⭐⭐

Changing your position to be in the optimal range to get a stun hit. Usually by using the S key {S-Hold or S-Tap}.
You could do it with a/d as well but its harder and less effective in most cases.
Can be combined with other techniques. For example using an s-crit to reposition yourself for a stun.

❌ Worst Scenarios: VS Sprinthits, Any kind of crit beside NoKb Crit

📝 NoKb Technique

Risk ⭐⭐☆
Reward ⭐⭐☆

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

Jump while sprinting forward right as someone hits you. Has to be done with perfect timing by knowing your opponent's hit timing.

Hit the target with your crosshair at 90% charge or lower.

Technique Creator - LoCr
Name Creator - LoCr

📝 Damage / NoKb Technique

Risk ⭐⭐⭐
Reward ⭐⭐☆

title: basic-knowledge
html:
⚔️ Hit Types ⚔️

There are 5 different hits, all with individual sound.

Sweep Hit- 90%-100% charged crosshair, and just hit normally, you must cancel your sprint hit so you can achieve this; it will do damage to everyone in range of the hit.

Sprint Hit- 90%-100% charged crosshair, hit while sprinting to gain extra knockback on the opponent.

Critical Hit- 90%-100% charged crosshair hit while falling for excess damage, will give special particles.

Pick Hit- 0%-90% charged crosshair, doing less damage and knockback.

Standard Hit- 90%-100% charged crosshair, hit while jumping but without sprint [not useful in combat].

📝Game Rules 📝

  • Reach- The max range is 3 blocks.
  • Momentum- Moving forward = more range. Moving back or standing in place = less range.
  • Knockback Rule 1- If you sprint while facing the target, you get less knockback [while falling too].
  • Knockback Rule 2- Hitting while taking KB and sprinting at the same time, reduces your remaining KB by 40%.
  • Crouch- Decreases your hitbox size.
  • Priority- Sprinthits have priority over Standard hits, Crits, and Sweeps.

🧑‍🏫Terms 🧑‍🏫

  • First Hit- The first hit you land on your opponent when both in a neutral position.
  • Hit Advantage- Whenever you are in a position where you can hit your opponent first.
  • Hit Priority- Initially gained through landing your hit first, which gives you control over the fight. It can shift between players mid trade depending on how things play out .
  • Stun- Getting a hit that gets your opponent stunned - unable to hit you back and move towards you.
  • Knock Away- a Sprinthit that knocks people away from you.
  • Double Hit- Whenever you knock someone away and able to hit them again without getting hit back.
  • Crit Chain- Getting multiple crits in a row.
  • Stun Combo- Getting multiple stun hits in a row.

⚔️ Playstyle ⚔️

‼️ Your playstyle should always be flexible. But when you fight players the first time, there is going to be a more safer approach to go for. Once you learn their patterns and decision making, you can change your playstyle accordingly to beat what they do.

📋General Playstyle Tips📋

  • Focus on first hits. Make sure you either hit your opponent first, or at least at the same time as they hit you. If you miss a first hit, it gives your opponent a chance to combo you, or take control over the fight at times.
  • You would usually want to lead with crits if possible, there are some situations where ground hits can be better, but ideally you should focus more on critting.
  • Avoid getting critted "for free" at all cost. Try to be the one who crits first and avoid getting hit by a crit while you're on the ground.
  • In some situations, when critting its better to release W in the last second, for max reach and taking the lowest knockback you can. Mainly good when going for a crit as a first hit, or doing NoKb Crits.

🥊 Playstyle Structure 🥊

🔻 When the fight is in an equal state 🔻

If both are jumping in at around the same time, you should usually be using Standard Crits. You're gonna want to be the first one to pull off a counter and gain a Hit Advantage, Hit Priority or a Stun.
- For example - finding a window to S-Crit, Deflect, use a Crit Trade Counter [explained in advanced channels] or anything else that fits the situation best.
- Also, you need to be ready to hold S in case your opponent manages to properly deflect you mid-trade, to avoid taking extra damage.

🔻 When you're the aggressor 🔻

📋Lead with a Crit. Now you have two options --->

  • Going for Standard Crits: If they do ANYTHING that isn't a Crit Deflection, you should win the trade.
    ‼️But... if they choose to Deflect you, you're gonna have to react fast and hold S to avoid getting countered and taking damage.

  • Going for a NoKb Crit: If they try to Deflect it normally - you win. You have full control and you can choose whether you want to attempt a Falling Sprinthit Followup to your NoKb Crit, or just keep on NoKb Critting.
    ‼️But... this one is a bit dangerous because -
    1. They can lead with a S-Hold Deflection, which is very hard to react to in time if you choose to do a NoKb Crit. That can lead to you getting combo'd. [You need to land very close to them for them to not be able to s-hold deflect you]
    2. They can lead with a Double Crit, which will even out the damage, making you lose the advantage you had by hitting them first.

📋If you happen to lead with a ground hit, it should mainly be when you're either too close to the opponent to be able to crit them, or if you try to catch your opponent off guard [for example straightline sprinthitting them when they're mid-air trying to crit you, etc...].

🔻 When you're the defender 🔻

📋Avoid as much damage as you can whilst trying to get a Hit Advantage --->

1. Hit Dodging - Allows you to achieve a first hit, which gives you control over the fight [very crucial].
Playing for hit dodging requires you to be in a more defensive position, which will make it harder to hit you on its own.
- You can also jump in as soon as they get near. Playing defensively will make it easier to land your hits.

2. What happens if you get hit? --->
‼️When you get critted while you're on the ground, you should be leading with either a Crit Deflection or an S-Hold Deflection.

Why is that? --->

  • You can't possibly know if your opponent is going to go for Standard Crits or NoKb Crits. If you choose to Double Crit on your first hit as they go for Standard Crits, you will get out traded for sure and possibly take a lot of damage. Not worth the risk.

  • Both a Deflection and an S-Hold Deflection will minimize the amount of damage you're gonna take and are a lot less risky to go for.

❓So which one you choose to use between Deflection and S-Hold Deflection? --->

  • S-Hold Deflection --> When your opponent lands far away from you [mid-long range]. This will ensure that whether they use Standard Crits, OR mid-long range NoKb Crits - they will get knocked away.
    You can use Repositioning before an S-Hold Deflection if possible, to ensure you get that mid-long range
    ‼️BUT.... if you use an S-Hold Deflection from a close range, it could give your opponent enough distance to be able to stun you with a Falling Sprinthit after their NoKb Crit.
    So ---> If they land close to you, you are FORCED to use a Crit Deflection.

  • If you go for a regular Crit Deflection as they go for a short range NoKb Crit, Use a "Double Crit" on your next hit to counter their next NoKb Crit.

If they choose to Deflect it to counter you, make sure you hold S in time, and at least it resets the fight and WILL get you out of that bad spot.

What happens once you fight them once twice three times four times etc.... ⁉️

  • When you reach a point where you learn how they play, you can start changing the structure that is mentioned above.

❗FOR EXAMPLE ---> You CAN go for a Double Crit on your first hit if you already KNOW that their playstyle is revolved more around NoKb Crits, to be able to immediately counter it.

✅ You can pretty much change anything up depending on the player you play against. Learn their playstyle, learn the way they think, and adapt properly.

🚀 Extras - Situational Counters to Defensive Players --->

- Play defensively like they do - it will kill their advantage and its a safe way to read your opponent a little before you choose what you want to do.

- Critting defensive players is harder because you can't really crit them from the normal range that you would usually go for when you crit. Therefore just run in a straightline to them and crit them from a closer range than you usually would. Also, release "W" a bit later [right before the hit] for a max range crit.

- Do a double jump to close the gap faster. Can be good but might also be a bit risky at times.

- Sometimes it can be good catching them off guard with either a sprinthit, uppercut, or a falling sprinthit in a sudden movement when they don't expect it.

📋Final Thoughts📋

Being too calculated in PvP could hold you back to an extent...

So i would only use this specific channel IF --->
- You've learned the techniques mentioned in my guide and still feel like you don't understand what you're supposed to do.
- You already have a solid playstyle but you feel like you have some weaknesses and you're not sure about what you do wrong.
- You feel like you reached a peak and you want to make sure that you do things correctly.

# ⚔️ __Playstyle__ ⚔️
‼️ Your playstyle should always be flexible. But when you fight players the first time, there is going to be a more safer approach to go for. Once you learn their patterns and decision making, you can change your playstyle accordingly to beat what they do.

## 📋__General Playstyle Tips__📋 
- Focus on first hits. Make sure you either hit your opponent first, or at least at the same time as they hit you. If you miss a first hit, it gives your opponent a chance to combo you, or take control over the fight at times.
- You would usually want to lead with crits if possible, there are some situations where ground hits can be better, but ideally you should focus more on critting.
- Avoid getting critted "for free" at all cost. Try to be the one who crits first and avoid getting hit by a crit while you're on the ground.
- In some situations, when critting its better to release W in the last second, for max reach and taking the lowest knockback you can. Mainly good when going for a crit as a first hit, or doing NoKb Crits.

# 🥊 __Playstyle Structure__ 🥊

## 🔻 **__When the fight is in an equal state__** 🔻 
If both are jumping in at around the same time, you should usually be using **Standard Crits**. You're gonna want to be the first one to pull off a counter and gain a __Hit Advantage, Hit Priority or a Stun.__
- For example - finding a window to **S-Crit**, **Deflect**, use a **Crit Trade Counter** [explained in advanced channels] or anything else that fits the situation best.
- Also, you need to be ready to **hold S** in case your opponent manages to properly deflect you mid-trade, to avoid taking extra damage.

## 🔻 **__When you're the aggressor__** 🔻 

 📋__**Lead with a Crit. Now you have two options**__ **--->**

- __**Going for Standard Crits**__: If they do ANYTHING that isn't a **Crit Deflection**, you should win the trade.
‼️But... if they choose to **Deflect** you, you're gonna have to react fast and **hold S** to avoid getting countered and taking damage. 

- __**Going for a NoKb Crit**__: If they try to **Deflect** it normally - you win. You have full control and you can choose whether you want to attempt a **Falling Sprinthit Followup** to your **NoKb Crit**, or just keep on **NoKb Critting**.
‼️__But... this one is a bit dangerous because__ -
`1.` They can lead with a **S-Hold Deflection**, which is very hard to react to in time if you choose to do a **NoKb Crit**. That can lead to you getting combo'd. [You need to land very close to them for them to not be able to s-hold deflect you]
`2.` They can lead with a **Double Crit**, which will even out the damage, making you lose the advantage you had by hitting them first.

📋If you happen to lead with a ground hit, it should mainly be when you're either too close to the opponent to be able to crit them, or if you try to catch your opponent off guard [for example straightline sprinthitting them when they're mid-air trying to crit you, etc...].

## 🔻 **__When you're the defender__** 🔻

📋__**Avoid as much damage as you can whilst trying to get a Hit Advantage**__ --->

`1.` __Hit Dodging__ - Allows you to achieve a first hit, which gives you control over the fight [very crucial].
Playing for hit dodging requires you to be in a more defensive position, which will make it harder to hit you on its own.
- You can also jump in as soon as they get near. Playing defensively will make it easier to land your hits.

`2.` __What happens if you get hit?__ --->
‼️When you get critted while you're on the ground, you should be leading with either a __Crit Deflection__ or an __S-Hold Deflection__.

__Why is that__? --->

- You can't possibly know if your opponent is going to go for **Standard Crits** or **NoKb Crits**. If you choose to **Double Crit** on your first hit as they go for **Standard Crits**, you will get out traded for sure and possibly take a lot of damage. Not worth the risk.

- Both a __Deflection__ and an __S-Hold Deflection__ will minimize the amount of damage you're gonna take and are a lot less risky to go for.

❓**So which one you choose to use between Deflection and S-Hold Deflection?** --->

- __S-Hold Deflection__ --> When your opponent lands far away from you [mid-long range]. This will ensure that whether they use **Standard Crits**, OR **mid-long range NoKb Crits** - they will get knocked away.
_You can use Repositioning before an S-Hold Deflection if possible, to ensure you get that mid-long range_
‼️**BUT**.... if you use an **S-Hold Deflection** from a close range, it could give your opponent enough distance to be able to stun you with a **Falling Sprinthit** after their NoKb Crit.
So ---> If they land close to you, you are FORCED to use a **Crit Deflection**.

- If you go for a regular **Crit Deflection** as they go for a **short range NoKb Crit**, Use a "**Double Crit**" on your next hit to counter their next **NoKb Crit**.

❗__FOR EXAMPLE__ ---> You CAN go for a **Double Crit** on your first hit if you already KNOW that their playstyle is revolved more around **NoKb Crits**, to be able to immediately counter it.

✅ **__You can pretty much change anything up depending on the player you play against. Learn their playstyle, learn the way they think, and adapt properly__.**

`-` Play defensively like they do - it will kill their advantage and its a safe way to read your opponent a little before you choose what you want to do.

`-` Critting defensive players is harder because you can't really crit them from the normal range that you would usually go for when you crit. `-` Do a double jump to close the gap faster. Can be good but might also be a bit risky at times.

title: important-figures
html:
📝About Me 📝

I started playing 1.9 sword right when the version came out and was the first HT1 and the best player of the older era of sword (2016-2017-2018).

I was the first to truly understand how sword pvp works and how all the techniques and all the counters come together. I was consistently the first one to figure out what the best players of each era did "intuitively" and gave their tactics a meaning by pointing out how they're performed and giving them names, as well as inventing some important techniques on my own, and then popularizing all those techniques to everyone. I was able to write a full guide all on my own that puts everything together in a way that makes sense.

Although i haven't been an active player for a long time, i think sword has been fully figured out at this point, which will make this guide up to date at any point in time. And if something new DOES come out, i will get notified and will update the guide if needed.

I was the first one to find out about certain techniques: "Crit Deflection", NoKb Combo, "Punish Crit Reaction", Baits, Side Sweeps, Followup Sweep, Backaway Sweep, Punish Sweep as well as giving names to techniques that everybody uses today, like Punish Crits, NoKb Crits, Double Crits, Crit Deflection, Stun Hit.

I've taught countless of people in the past, including a bunch of tier 1 players, and fought all of the best players to ever play sword.

I was the first one to start the concept of 1.9 FFA server that does tournaments back in 2017.

In 2018-2022 i was a Network Owner along with Encz.

Also, invented the term "Combat Master" that is used in the tierlist (Marlow further developed the whole concept though).

🗡️ Other Important Figures in Sword History 🗡️

  • LoCr - Invented important techniques when 1.9 PvP came out [2016]. Such as figuring out how to properly use - Sprinthits [W-Taps + S-Taps], Crits, Sprint Crits, Hit Dodging, Stun Combos, Crit Combos and gave them names that people use until this day Sprinthit, Sprint Crit, Pick hits. He was also the person who taught me how things work back in 2016.
    LoCr was also a "combat master" level player back when he played [which was before the rank was created].

  • Monkss - Invented Uppercuts [2018].

  • TryH4rdd - Invented the best playstyle in sword [2019]. Combined sword tactics with perfect synergy which made everyone copy the way he plays. The playstyle has been significantly improved since then, but still to this day, it contains the fundamentals TryH4rdd created. TryH4rdd invented "Double Crits" which is a counter to "NoKb Crits".
    TryH4rdd was also the best pot pvper back when he played, and brought many sword techniques to pot.

🔻Honorable Mentions🔻

  • TikiGamesTV - First person to abuse a defensive playstyle.
  • Stumpie - The first person to main a crit playstyle.
  • michaelcycle00 - Invented the Turnback Movement
  • Time_4_PvP - The first one to bring Jump Resets to 1.9 PvP.

🧑‍🏫 Every name mentioned in this channel has contributed SIGNIFICANTLY to the development of Sword PvP, popularized techniques, created metas and sped up the learning process of 1.9 pvp since the moment it came out until now.

title: defensive-tactics
html:
🪃Hit Dodging🪃

1. Dodging First Hits -
Walk back right before the opponent gets in range to hit you to dodge their incoming hit. Has to be done from the right distance with good timing.
If you play defensively and letting the opponent come to you it makes it harder for them to hit you and easier for you to dodge. After dodging successfully, you can either attempt a stun combo or go for a crit.

‼️Countered by Falling Sprinthit‼️

  • You can also dodge first hits by flicking, strafing and sprint jumping to the side to avoid your opponent's first hit. This variant is risky and unreliable if predicted - Avoid using it multiple times.

2. Baits - Walk OR jump towards your opponent, baiting them to go in and then walk back immediately to dodge their hit, giving you a Hit Advantage. This is also the best counter to defensive players, getting them out of the defensive position, leaving them exposed to a hit.

3. "The Turn Back" Movement -
1. When you see that your opponent is about to attack you, turn back away from your opponent for a second to dodge the hit, and then turn back towards your opponent and attack (better going for a crit after turning back - it is more efficient)

  1. You can use this in a middle of a trade - sometimes you will have a very short period of time during a trade when you can use the turn back movement to dodge your opponent's hit or get yourself a hit advantage.

🏃‍♂️Escaping Stun hits / Combos🏃‍♂️

There are 3 ways to escape stun combos depending on the situation.

1. Hold S - This is the most common way to escape stun combos.

2. S-Hold Jump - Jump while holding S. This will increase the knockback you recieve. Use this ONLY when you feel like you need that extra knockback for them to not be able to reach you.
- This will only work if done on hits like Deflection, that you can jump before they happen.
- Mainly useful VS high ms.

3. Turn back completely - In some scenarios you will have to turn back completely and run to be able to get out of your opponent's reach.

Clips: Holding S, S-Hold Jumps, Turn Back

🚀 Movement 🚀

Movement can be used for --->
1. Making your opponent miss hits.
2. Gain distance that is necessary for a stun hit.

  • Usually you wouldn't want to move around when there's a risk of you getting stunned by your opponent (straightlining will decrease your knockback, reducing the chance of getting stunned). So its better to attempt it when you're close enough to the opponent to not get stunned, OR when your opponent misses a hit, you can make them miss further if you start moving around them and switching directions to mess with their aim.
  • Works best with crits and sweeps, but can also work with sprinthits.
  • There are unlimited possibilities when it comes to Movement patterns and here are a few examples 🔻

⭐ Strafe ⭐

1. Short Strafe - Strafes with faster a/d movements
2. Side-To-Side Strafe - Switch the strafing direction after every hit
3. Circle Strafe - Strafe to one side, circling around the target.

These techniques can be used with W-Taps, S-Taps, Pausing W-Taps, Crits, Uppercuts or Sweeps

‼️Important -

  • When you strafe its a little harder to hit you, but you will also receive more KB which can result in you getting stunned and combo'd.
  • Can be used for dodging hits OR for spacing purposes [Sometimes strafing to a certain direction could get you to the distance that you need to be able to stun someone].
  • If you choose to strafe, it should ONLY be in scenarios where you can't get punished for it.
  • Can strafing be useful? Yes it can be. But... you could probably get tier 1 without strafing at all, which turns strafing into a personal preference.
  • There are unlimited possibilities when it comes to Strafe, and here are a few examples 🔻

# 🪃__**Hit Dodging**__🪃

`1.` __**Dodging First Hits**__ -
Walk back right before the opponent gets in range to hit you to dodge their incoming hit. Has to be done from the right distance with good timing.
If you play defensively and letting the opponent come to you it makes it harder for them to hit you and easier for you to dodge. After dodging successfully, you can either attempt a stun combo or go for a crit.

‼️**__Countered by Falling Sprinthit__**‼️

* You can also dodge first hits by flicking, strafing and sprint jumping to the side to avoid your opponent's first hit. **This variant is risky and unreliable if predicted - Avoid using it multiple times**.

`2.` __**Baits**__ - __Walk__ OR __jump__ towards your opponent, baiting them to go in and then walk back immediately to dodge their hit, giving you a Hit Advantage. This is also the best counter to defensive players, getting them out of the defensive position, leaving them exposed to a hit.

`3.` __**"The Turn Back" Movement**__ -
1. When you see that your opponent is about to attack you, turn back away from your opponent for a second to dodge the hit, and then turn back towards your opponent and attack (better going for a crit after turning back - it is more efficient)

2. You can use this in a **middle of a trade** - sometimes you will have a very short period of time during a trade when you can use the turn back movement to dodge your opponent's hit or get yourself a hit advantage.

# 🏃‍♂️__Escaping Stun hits / Combos__🏃‍♂️

There are 3 ways to escape stun combos depending on the situation.

`1`. __Hold S__ - This is the most common way to escape stun combos. 

`2`. __S-Hold Jump__ - Jump while holding S. This will increase the knockback you recieve. Use this ONLY when you feel like you need that extra knockback for them to not be able to reach you.
- This will only work if done on hits like Deflection, that you can jump before they happen.
- Mainly useful VS high ms.

`3`. __Turn back completely__ - In some scenarios you will have to turn back completely and run to be able to get out of your opponent's reach.

_Clips: Holding S, S-Hold Jumps, Turn Back_

# 🚀 __**Movement**__ 🚀 
__Movement can be used for__ --->
`1`. Making your opponent miss hits.
`2`. Gain distance that is necessary for a stun hit.

- Usually you wouldn't want to move around when there's a risk of you getting stunned by your opponent (straightlining will decrease your knockback, reducing the chance of getting stunned). So its better to attempt it when you're close enough to the opponent to not get stunned, OR when your opponent misses a hit, you can make them miss further if you start moving around them and switching directions to mess with their aim. 
- Works best with __crits__ and __sweeps__, but can also work with __sprinthits__.
- There are unlimited possibilities when it comes to Movement patterns and here are a few examples 🔻

# ⭐ **__Strafe__** ⭐

`1.` Short Strafe - Strafes with faster a/d movements 
`2.` Side-To-Side Strafe - Switch the strafing direction after every hit
`3.` Circle Strafe - Strafe to one side, circling around the target.

*These techniques can be used with __W-Taps, S-Taps, Pausing W-Taps, Crits, Uppercuts or Sweeps__*
### ‼️__Important__ -

- When you strafe its a little harder to hit you, but you will also receive more KB which can result in you getting stunned and combo'd.
- Can be used for dodging hits OR for spacing purposes [Sometimes strafing to a certain direction could get you to the distance that you need to be able to stun someone].
- If you choose to strafe, it should ONLY be in scenarios where you can't get punished for it.
- Can strafing be useful? Yes it can be. But... you could probably get tier 1 without strafing at all, which turns strafing into a personal preference.
- There are unlimited possibilities when it comes to Strafe, and here are a few examples 🔻

🎯 Punish Crit Reaction 🎯

Technique Creator - xYuvalx
Name Creator - xYuvalx

📝 Knockaway / Damage Technique

Risk ⭐⭐☆
Reward ⭐⭐☆

Objective- being able to know when your opponent wants to "Double Crit" or "NoKb Crit", and counter instantly.

First, you have to be able to recognize the difference between a Sprinthit hit timing and a Punish Crit hit timing.
How can you tell the difference?
A Punish Crit will be more delayed than a Sprinthit (since to punish crit, you have to hit while falling, and to Sprinthit you can hit while taking knockback) You have to learn how to spot the exact time when their hit delay changes to "a punish crit hit delay".

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

📋Double Crit Reaction -
A situation that happens often is when you Nokb Crit someone and they try to Sprinthit you away but then when they can't, they will decide to Double Crit you to try to counter your NoKb Crits. You have to recognize the change in the hit timing from the Sprinthit to the PunishCrit thats gonna turn into a Double Crit, and Sprinthit them away to counter their incoming Double Crit, potentially getting a combo off.
After you get good at this, you can react to people who use DoubleCrits right after your first hit on them.

📋NoKb Crit Reaction -
Some people will go for NoKb Crits after their punish crit, then you have to recognize it and react with a Double Crit instead of a sprinthit, to counter them.
*If they go for a Sprinthit after their punish crit, keep NoKb Critting them to counter the incoming Sprinthit.

✅ Best Scenarios: Depends on the reaction type
❌ Worst Scenarios: Depends on the reaction type

🔻 _ Clips: NoKb Crit Reaction Clip MISSING ATM, Double Crit Reaction_🔻

🎯 NoKb Combo 🎯

Name Creator - xYuvalx

📝 NoKb Technique

Risk ⭐⭐⭐
Reward ⭐⭐⭐

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

💥An advanced counter to "Crit Deflections". Combo with NoKb Crit into Jump Reset.

📋Whenever you crit your opponent while they're on the ground, they will either try to deflect your crit, or punish crit/double crit after you crit them.

▶️ What happens if your opponent chooses to go for a "Crit Deflection"?
Right after you land your Crit on them, use a Jump Reset on the incoming sprinthit. It will reduce your KB to literally 0. This will make it way harder to knock you away and will put you in a better position to out trade your opponent.

▶️ What happens if your opponent chooses to go for a "Punish Crit/Double Crit"?
You using a NoKb Crit into Jump Reset will put you in a position where you're already in the air because of the jump, allowing you to still get your second crit on them without getting countered.
*This will make it harder to aim though.

  • This move is hard to pull off successfully, you need to have good timing and understand your opponent's "crit deflection" timing. If you mess up the timing of this move you will end up getting knocked away, giving your opponent a chance to get a combo.

🔻When to use this move🔻
1. First Hits VS Deflection
2. In the middle of a NoKb Crit chain

🔻The only ways to counter this move🔻
1. Change the timing on your "crit deflection", making it so your opponent misses the timing of the "NoKb Combo" resulting in them getting knocked away.
2. Punish crit into a crit deflection. { Credit - QZ69 }

  • You can use it for multiple hits in a row, or you can use it once or twice and then move on to other things, situationally.

✅ Best Scenarios: VS Deflection
❌ Worst Scenarios: VS Inconsistent hit timing / Punish Crit into Deflection

🔻Clips: NoKb Combo, NoKb Combo Counters🔻

🎯 Falling Sprinthit Deflection[Crit Trade Counter] 🎯

📝 Knockaway Technique

Risk ⭐⭐☆
Reward ⭐⭐☆

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

📋When you and your opponent are about to crit eachother at the exact same time, let them crit you and then do a "falling sprinthit" instead of a crit, right after they land their crit on you [ Use a "crit deflection" timing ]. It will result in them getting knocked away, allowing you to start a combo.

  • Can be used either in the middle of a trade, or on first hits, right before the trade is about to start.
  • Its usually hard to "predict" when you and your opponent about ABOUT to crit eachother at the same time, therefore i would recommend first letting the situation occur, and do a Falling Sprinthit Deflection on the second crit of the exchange, expecting the following crit to land at the same time as well.
  • Which means: Crit at the exact same time --> Jump again --> letting them crit you --> Falling sprinthit deflection.

✅ Best Scenarios: When both you and your opponent are about to crit eachother at the same time.
❌ Worst Scenarios: Any other scenario.

🔻Clips: First hit Falling Sprinthit Deflection, Mid Trade Falling Sprinthit Defleciton🔻

🎯 Crouch Dodge 🎯

Name Creator - xYuvalx

📝 Escape Technique

Risk ⭐☆☆
Reward ⭐⭐☆
‼️ This move is only low risk if it is used in the way its supposed to be used - as a last resort!

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

Hold crouch right before your opponent is about to swing, to dodge their hit {crouching reduces your hitbox size}.

📋How to properly dodge using crouch?
- First off, you should NEVER rely on crouching because its not guarantied that you'll manage to dodge your opponent's hits every time and using it incorrectly might result in you taking unnecessary damage.
- The main use for it is when you're on the ground and your opponent is critting, since they have to look down to crit you and when you crouch the upper part of your hitbox becomes smaller. { ineffective against punish crits }

📋When is it good to crouch?
1. When you go for a straightline hit on them as they try to crit you. {Works when they're on the ground too, but less consistent}
2. Whenever you're in a position where you're gonna get critted regardless { For example, when they dodge your hit or when you just miss as they try to crit you } you can crouch as a last resort move to at least try to make it so there's a chance they'll miss their hit.

✅ Best Scenarios: As a LAST RESORT move, which means: if you stumbled upon a bad position and you will get hit anyways / If there is no risk using this move [example - you plan on going for a ground hit regardless]
❌ Worst Scenarios: Any other scenario.

Technique Creator - xYuvalx
Name Creator - xYuvalx

📝 Escape Technique

Risk ⭐☆☆
Reward ⭐⭐☆

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

This is an advanced strategy for avoiding combos -

▶️ Stun-Hit Prediction - When you are ABOUT to get stunned, and hold S immediately right on the hit that is supposed to stun you.
That will make it so your opponent loses their combo before they even started it.

▶️ Stun-Hit Reaction - Reacting to your opponent's spacing techniques and holding S before they can stun you. For example - when they try to reposition, or when they s-crit.

✅ Best Scenarios: When you predict you will get stunned by a hit.
❌ Worst Scenarios: X

html:
⚔️ Sweep ⚔️

Name Creator - LoCr

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

🪃 There are 2 ways of Sweeping🪃
Sprinthits have priority over sweeps. Therefore, to get a sweep you need to cancel the sprinthit first [or just not sprint]-

  1. Sprint Sweep - Hold "W" + Sprint and go for a combo. The first hit of the combo will always be a sprinthit, after you use your sprinthit, the rest of your hits will be sweeps until you reset your sprint.

  2. "W Release Sweeps" - Release "W" every time before you hit. IE release "W" --> Hit --> press "W" again.
    You could also strafe your opponent without touching "w" at all in some situations. usually better to do in the middle of a combo, don't start a combo this way

🔻Clips: W - Release Sweeps, Sprint Sweep🔻

🪃Single Sweep🪃

Name Creator - xYuvalx

📝 Damage Technique

Risk ⭐⭐☆
Reward ⭐⭐☆

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

📋Going for a SINGLE sweep, to make people miss their hit. Combine it with different types of hits, like sprinthits or crits, depending on the situation.

✅ Best Scenarios:
- When people get really close to you which could allow you to strafe out of their vision with the sweep.
- If they miss a hit, allowing you to make them miss further.

❌ Worst Scenarios: Long range.

🪃Sweep Combo🪃

📝 Damage Technique

Risk ⭐⭐☆
Reward ⭐⭐☆

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

📋Strafing while using sweeps will significantly increase the opponent's chances of missing hits on you. Aim is heavily reliant on predictions, and its very hard to predict where your character is going to be when you strafe with sweeps.

  • Sweep combos will USUALLY be good if you're in a position where they already are unable to hit you. For example if you end up being behind them, or if they miss their hit on you and you're close enough to them to make sweeps effective.

  • This would only work if you're already in close range, and in some situations, could be better than sprinthits because sprinthits from a close range are easy to aim against, and also give your opponent the chance to hit select you. And if you sweep, you cannot be hit selected as long as you are close to them.

You can also change up the movement pattern once they are trying to recover their aim to mess them up further.

✅ Best Scenarios: Close range, When they miss their hit.
❌ Worst Scenarios: Long range.

🪃Punish Sweep🪃

Technique Creator - xYuvalx
Name Creator - iDexy

📝 Stun Technique

Risk ⭐☆☆
Reward ⭐⭐⭐

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

‼️A counter to Hit Select -
📋Sweep into Sprinthit. Sweep the opponent --> let them sprinthit you --> sprinthit them back to stun them.

  • Sweep the opponent when they try to hit select you. Your sweep will deal less KB than a sprinthit, which will make it so your opponent can't get enough range to stun you with their hit select. Now you are pushed back from your opponent's sprinthit, which puts you in the right range to stun them with your next sprinthit.
  • You could also go for Punish Sweeps while comboing people, it could confuse them and make it so they won't think they need to hold S to escape, allowing you to stay in control and deal a lot more damage to them.
  • Punish Sweeps will ONLY work if you have a Hit Priority.

✅ Best Scenarios: VS Hit Select
❌ Worst Scenarios: Any other time.

🪃Backaway Sweep🪃

Technique Creator - xYuvalx
Name Creator - xYuvalx

📝 Escape Technique

Risk ⭐☆☆
Reward ⭐⭐☆

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

📋Sweep into S-Crit. Sweep the opponent, let them hit you, then s-crit away.
This could be good if you want to disengage or gain a hit advantage.
- Works only when you have a "Hit Priority".

✅ Best Scenarios: When you hit a hit priority.
❌ Worst Scenarios: Any other occasion.

🪃Followup Sweep🪃

Technique Creator - xYuvalx
Name Creator - xYuvalx

📝 Damage Technique

Risk ⭐☆☆
Reward ⭐⭐☆

🔻 How to Perform 🔻

📋Holding W as people try to back away from your combos, to catch them with a Sweep.
Since sweeps deal less knockback, it will allow you to stay on people even if they hold S trying to escape your combo.
- This could be combined with a "Punish Sweep" to extend your combo. When you go in with a sweep people won't think they need to hold S to escape, which allows you to counter the incoming hit-select with a punish sweep and keep your combo going.
- This could be combined with "Backaway Sweep".

✅ Best Scenarios: When people hold S
❌ Worst Scenarios: When you don't predict correctly and they don't try to back away from your combo.

🔻Clips: Purple sword one by Kylaz🔻

# ⚔️ __**Sweep**__ ⚔️ 
_Name Creator_ - LoCr
## 🔻 __**How to Perform**__ 🔻 
🪃 __**There are 2 ways of Sweeping**__🪃 
Sprinthits have priority over sweeps. Therefore, to get a sweep you need to cancel the sprinthit first [or just not sprint]-

1. __Sprint Sweep__ - Hold "W" + Sprint and go for a combo. The first hit of the combo will always be a sprinthit, after you use your sprinthit, the rest of your hits will be sweeps until you reset your sprint.

2. __"W Release Sweeps"__ - Release "W" every time before you hit. IE release "W" --> Hit --> press "W" again. 
_You could also strafe your opponent without touching "w" at all in some situations. usually better to do in the middle of a combo, don't start a combo this way_

🔻_Clips: W - Release Sweeps, Sprint Sweep_🔻

# 🪃__**Single Sweep**__🪃
_Name Creator_ - xYuvalx
##  📝 Damage Technique
> Risk ⭐⭐<:star1:1360585436468346970>
> Reward ⭐⭐<:star1:1360585436468346970>

## 🔻 __**How to Perform**__ 🔻 
📋Going for a SINGLE sweep, to make people miss their hit. Combine it with different types of hits, like sprinthits or crits, depending on the situation.

✅ __Best Scenarios__: 
- When people get really close to you which could allow you to strafe out of their vision with the sweep.
 - If they miss a hit, allowing you to make them miss further.

❌ __Worst Scenarios__: Long range.

# 🪃__**Sweep Combo**__🪃 
##  📝 Damage Technique
> Risk ⭐⭐<:star1:1360585436468346970>
> Reward ⭐⭐<:star1:1360585436468346970>

## 🔻 __**How to Perform**__ 🔻 
📋Strafing while using sweeps will significantly increase the opponent's chances of missing hits on you. Aim is heavily reliant on predictions, and its very hard to predict where your character is going to be when you strafe with sweeps.

- Sweep combos will USUALLY be good if you're in a position where they already are unable to hit you. For example if you end up being behind them, or if they miss their hit on you and you're close enough to them to make sweeps effective.

- This would only work if you're already in close range, and in some situations, could be better than sprinthits because sprinthits from a close range are easy to aim against, and also give your opponent the chance to hit select you. And if you sweep, you cannot be hit selected __as long as you are close to them.__

You can also change up the movement pattern once they are trying to recover their aim to mess them up further.

✅ __Best Scenarios__: Close range, When they miss their hit.
❌ __Worst Scenarios__: Long range.

# 🪃__**Punish Sweep**__🪃
_Technique Creator_ - xYuvalx
_Name Creator_ - iDexy
##  📝 Stun Technique
> Risk ⭐<:star1:1360585436468346970><:star1:1360585436468346970>
> Reward ⭐⭐⭐

## 🔻 __**How to Perform**__ 🔻 
‼️**__A counter to Hit Select__** -
📋__Sweep__ into __Sprinthit__. Sweep the opponent --> let them sprinthit you --> sprinthit them back to stun them.

- Sweep the opponent when they try to hit select you. Your sweep will deal less KB than a sprinthit, which will make it so your opponent can't get enough range to stun you with their hit select. Now you are pushed back from your opponent's sprinthit, which puts you in the right range to stun them with your next sprinthit.
- You could also go for Punish Sweeps while comboing people, it could confuse them and make it so they won't think they need to hold S to escape, allowing you to stay in control and deal a lot more damage to them.
- __Punish Sweeps will ONLY work if you have a Hit Priority__.

✅ __Best Scenarios__: VS **Hit Select**
❌ __Worst Scenarios__: Any other time.

# 🪃**__Backaway Sweep__**🪃
_Technique Creator_ - xYuvalx
_Name Creator_ - xYuvalx
##  📝 Escape Technique
> Risk ⭐<:star1:1360585436468346970><:star1:1360585436468346970>
> Reward ⭐⭐<:star1:1360585436468346970>

## 🔻 __**How to Perform**__ 🔻 
📋Sweep into S-Crit. Sweep the opponent, let them hit you, then s-crit away.
This could be good if you want to disengage or gain a hit advantage.
- Works only when you have a "Hit Priority".

✅ __Best Scenarios__: When you hit a hit priority.
❌ __Worst Scenarios__: Any other occasion.

# 🪃**__Followup Sweep__**🪃
_Technique Creator_ - xYuvalx
_Name Creator_ - xYuvalx
##  📝 Damage Technique
> Risk ⭐<:star1:1360585436468346970><:star1:1360585436468346970>
> Reward ⭐⭐<:star1:1360585436468346970>

## 🔻 __**How to Perform**__ 🔻 
📋Holding W as people try to back away from your combos, to catch them with a Sweep. 
Since sweeps deal less knockback, it will allow you to stay on people even if they hold S trying to escape your combo.
- This could be combined with a "Punish Sweep" to extend your combo. When you go in with a sweep people won't think they need to hold S to escape, which allows you to counter the incoming hit-select with a punish sweep and keep your combo going.
- This could be combined with "Backaway Sweep".

✅ __Best Scenarios__: When people hold S
❌ __Worst Scenarios__: When you don't predict correctly and they don't try to back away from your combo.

# 🪃__**Back Sweep [Crit Trade Counter]**__🪃 
##  📝 Stun Technique
> Risk ⭐<:star1:1360585436468346970><:star1:1360585436468346970>
> Reward ⭐⭐⭐

## 🔻 __**How to Perform**__ 🔻 
📋When you and your opponent are about to crit eachother at the exact same time, let them crit you while holding S and use a sweep on them after they land the crit on you. It will result in them getting stunned, granting you a hit advantage.

- Can be used either in the middle of a trade, or on first hits, right before the trade is about to start.
- Its usually hard to "predict" when you and your opponent are ABOUT to crit eachother at the same time, therefore i would recommend first letting the situation occur, and then use a Back Sweep on the second crit of the exchange. Which means: Crit at the exact same time --> Jump again --> letting them crit you --> do a Back Sweep.

✅ __Best Scenarios__: When both you and your opponent are about to crit eachother at the same time.
❌ __Worst Scenarios__: Any other scenario.

_Technique Creator_ - xYuvalx
_Name Creator_ - xYuvalx
##  📝 Escape Technique
> Risk ⭐<:star1:1360585436468346970><:star1:1360585436468346970>
> Reward ⭐⭐⭐

## 🔻 __**How to Perform**__ 🔻 
💥 This is an advanced counter to people who rush in aggressively (with NoKb crits, aggressive straightline, etc).

📋When you know that someone is going to rush into you aggressively  [usually with a NoKb move], Hold W and run into them, and then AFTER you get hit, let go of W, and  __hold__ ONLY "D" or "A" depending on your position, and turn towards them then hit them with a sweep.

- This move is meant to make your opponent completely lose their aim and get you out of a bad scenario. It won't always work, but it's still 100% the best move to go for in specific situations, especially because this is a very low risk move.

- This move will only work when - your opponent uses a low KB hit - for example: a crit. OR when they make your KB stop - for example: Sprinthitting you too fast while walking forward aggressively.

✅ __Best Scenarios__: VS players who rush in aggressively with moves such as NoKb Crits or aggressive straightlines, etc...
❌ __Worst Scenarios__: When they don't rush into you.
